full_judgment: 16. It is at this juncture that this Court finds merit in Ms. Rabia Bhuiyan's submission that an overly reliant approach on the strict application of objective standards of classification and/or conversion of loans meets its limitation in the circumstances above and it became prudent for the Bank to draw on its privilege under the Master Circular to rely instead on certain subjective criteria. It is this Court's finding that this is an avenue reasonably and fairly pursued by the Bank leading to the issuance of the impugned Order of 16.8.2010. Indeed, the Master Circular permits of "qualitative judgments" to be arrived at for debt/loan classification when the facts themselves do not permit of neat classifications predicated an objective criteria. The line of demarcation enabling any bank to cross over from an objective evaluation mechanism to one permitting of subjected assessment, this Court further finds, is defined preliminarily by the element of uncertainty brought on by a borrower's conduct vis-a-vis the creditor bank.
